monthly_review.summary: September shows a sharp drop in volume and cadence, coupled with a notable rise in Zone 4 work and aerobic TE — consistent with accumulated fatigue or premature intensity introduction without adequate base support.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence dropped 10 spm month-on-month — the largest single change — and aligns with rising aerobic TE (+0.4%) and falling efficiency (+0.51 ml/kg/km), indicating deteriorating neuromuscular coordination under fatigue.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 51.3 km, 16.8 km across 3 sessions would require ~5.6 km/session at or above current average pace — but compromised readiness and declining efficiency make this inadvisable; chasing volume now risks injury or further fatigue accumulation.

insights.title: Cadence collapse mirrors aerobic decoupling trend
insights.body: Cadence fell from 149 spm (Aug) to 139 spm (Sep), while avg aerobic TE rose from 2.6% to 3.0% — both suggest reduced running economy under load, especially given stride length variability (e.g., 65.7 cm on 8/23 vs 101.8 cm on 9/3) and ground contact time spikes (385 ms on 8/23, 389 ms on 9/1).

insights.title: Zone 4 workload surged without Z5 compensation or Z1 recovery buffer
insights.body: Z4 % jumped from 8% (Aug) to 27% (Sep), while Z1 dropped from 43% to 25% — a 18-point swing toward high-intensity work despite no Z5 effort (still 2%), suggesting poorly balanced stress without adequate low-intensity recovery foundation.

insights.title: Efficiency decline coincides with HR elevation and pace improvement
insights.body: Avg pace improved (+16 sec/km) while avg HR rose (+5 bpm) and efficiency worsened (+0.51 ml/kg/km) — classic sign of reduced aerobic efficiency: more cardiac effort for less mechanical return.

recommendations.action: Complete 3x 30-min Zone 1 walks or very easy jogs (HR ≤115 bpm, pace ≥12:00 min/km) on Mon/Wed/Fri — no distance target, only HR adherence.
recommendations.reason: Z1 volume has collapsed (25% this month vs 43% last month); rebuilding autonomic resilience requires consistent low-HR stimulus when readiness is compromised.

recommendations.action: Perform daily 10-min parasympathetic priming: 4-7-8 breathing + supine leg elevation (feet on wall) immediately after waking and before bed.
recommendations.reason: Missing HRV and sleep data necessitates proactive nervous system regulation; this counters elevated avg HR (+5 bpm) and rising aerobic TE.

recommendations.action: Skip all pace-, power-, or HR-targeted runs until next Garmin recovery metric sync — replace with perceived exertion only (RPE ≤2/10) for any movement.
recommendations.reason: Without HRV, sleep, or recovery balance data, objective thresholds are unsafe; subjective effort preserves autonomy while preventing inadvertent overload.

risk_flags.action: Pause all interval, tempo, and hill work until cadence stabilizes ≥145 spm and aerobic TE ≤2.5%

risk_flags.evidence: Z4 % = 27% (up from 8% in Aug) while Z1 = 25% (down from 43%) and no Z5 efforts recorded
risk_flags.action: Reduce Z4 frequency to ≤1x/week and restore Z1 to ≥40% of monthly volume before reintroducing Z4
